caption: Three of these debit orders I forgot I ever signed. Do you check yours or just trust them?

slides.title:
The R2 980 in debit
orders I forgot about,
on R18 400 p/m
Living in Kariega
slides.body:
Female, 36
Divorced, one son (12)
Job: Debtors clerk, motor dealership
Net salary: R18 400 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: I moved here after the divorce. The complex has a gate and he likes the pool.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Monthly shop at Shoprite, top-ups at the corner shop
slides.body: I plan the menu on Sunday. By Wednesday the plan is gone.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: A small car for a small salary. I did not argue with myself on this one.

slides.title: Petrol
slides.includes: Work and school run, no long trips
slides.body: I live four kilometres from work and still spend R1 400. The school run is the reason.

slides.title: Forgotten debit orders
slides.includes: A gym I last used in March, two apps, a magazine, an old insurance top-up, a cloud storage plan
slides.body: I added it up after I printed the statement. I had to sit down.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: prepaid electricity, school costs, funeral policy, stokvel, airtime, black tax
slides.body: Six lines that came to R3 030. Black tax is R1 000 of it, and it's the one I'd never cancel.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R18 400. If I had cancelled the forgotten ones in March I'd have R2 980 more every month.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and its recurring expense detection pulled out every debit order.

The gym was the one that hurt.

No bank login needed.
